target.title: fix(macos): fit onboarding window on short screens
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98674.

The macOS onboarding window used a fixed preferred content height and `window.center()`, so on short visible desktop areas the first-run window could extend below the screen and hide the bottom setup/navigation action.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes onboarding window placement through the existing `WindowPlacement.centeredFrame` helper so the actual NSWindow frame is clamped to the active screen visible frame before display. The SwiftUI root view now allows its height to shrink between the onboarding minimum and preferred height, so the clamped window can adapt instead of insisting on the full preferred height.

## User Impact

Users on shorter displays or desktops with reduced visible height should be able to see and click the onboarding bottom actions instead of getting stuck during first-run setup.

## Evidence

- Added `WindowPlacementTests` coverage for onboarding frame clamping on a 690pt short visible frame and for preserving preferred height on tall screens.
- `git diff --check`
- Attempted: `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter WindowPlacementTests` and `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter OnboardingViewSmokeTests`; both are blocked locally because `apps/macos` requires Swift tools 6.2.0 while this machine has Apple Swift 6.1.

target.title: fix(slack): log native progress stream start failures instead of silently swallowing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When native Slack progress streaming starts, overlapping progress callbacks can await the same in-flight `startSlackStream` promise. The **initiating** `updateNativeProgressStream()` path already reports failures via `runtime.error`, but the prior PR added a second `logVerbose` in the waiter catch — duplicating diagnostics for one rejection.

## Changes

- **Remove duplicate waiter logging** — `waitForNativeProgressStreamStart()` keeps a silent catch that only marks `streamFailed` and returns `false`.
- **Improve single-owner diagnostic** — initiating `updateNativeProgressStream()` now reports `start` vs `update` phase in the existing `runtime.error` message.
- **Add production-equivalent overlap regression** — uses the real `createChannelProgressDraftGate` with staggered overlapping progress callbacks; asserts exactly **one** `runtime.error` and **no** waiter `logVerbose` duplicate.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `94aad230`

**Regression tests:**
```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts \
  -t "native Slack progress start fails|overlapping native progress"
→ 2 passed
```

**Runtime proof (redacted):**
```json
{
  "scenario": "single runtime.error owner reports native progress stream start failure; overlapping waiter does not add logVerbose duplicate",
  "vitestExitCode": 0,
  "highlights": ["Test Files  1 passed (1)", "Tests  2 passed | 85 skipped (87)"]
}
```

**Lint / typecheck:** oxlint + tsgo on touched surfaces — clean

## Review

- ClawSweeper P1/P2 addressed: no duplicate waiter log, single error owner, production-equivalent overlap coverage + proof
- AI-assisted: Yes
